edges.description: Haploinsufficiency: one functional allele remains, and the mutant transcript is largely degraded, so less TANC2 protein reaches the postsynaptic density.
intermediate_mechanisms: Nonsense-mediated decay of the mutant transcript for premature stops outside the last coding exon
edges.target: Reduced TANC2 Protein at the Postsynaptic Density

edges.description: TANC2 binds mTOR and inhibits it, so less TANC2 means less inhibition.
edges.source: Reduced TANC2 Protein at the Postsynaptic Density

edges.description: TANC2, with liprin-alpha, recruits KIF1A-transported dense core vesicles to postsynaptic sites; losing the scaffold removes that capture.
edges.source: Reduced TANC2 Protein at the Postsynaptic Density
edges.target: Loss of KIF1A Dense Core Vesicle Capture at Spines

edges.description: With the brake gone, both complexes are hyperactive in the haploinsufficient animal.
Synaptic deficits accompany the hyperactivity and are reversed with it.
edges.target: Altered Dendritic Spine and Excitatory Synapse Development

edges.description: The zebrafish knockout expands the glutamatergic population selectively. The step from altered spine and synapse development to a change in population size is not established, and the intermediates are not known.
edges.source: Altered Dendritic Spine and Excitatory Synapse Development

edges.description: Raised seizure susceptibility, reported after TANC2 knockdown in Drosophila and manifesting clinically as epilepsy in about half of reported patients. The fly result is contradicted by an earlier knockdown in the same organism, so this edge carries both.
intermediate_mechanisms: Increased network excitability from the shifted excitatory-inhibitory balance

edges.description: The hyperactivity is measured in the heterozygous animal, which is the human genotype, and the pharmacological reversal closes the loop.
edges.limitations: Measured in mouse brain. No study has measured mTORC1 or mTORC2 activity in tissue or cells from a patient with a TANC2 variant, so the signalling state of the human disorder is inferred from this model rather than observed.

edges.description: The selective expansion of glutamatergic neurons with GABAergic and glycinergic populations unaffected is measured directly in this model.
edges.limitations: A homozygous knockout, where the human disease is heterozygous, so the dose is not the disease's. The behavioural readouts are also fish analogues of social and sleep phenotypes rather than the human cognitive and language features.

nodes.description: Dendritic spine and excitatory synapse development is disturbed. The TANC family's PDZ-binding C terminus is required for these proteins to increase spine and synapse density, so both the reduced-protein route and the motif-deleting route converge here. The direction of the change in patients is deliberately not asserted: what has been measured is that overexpression of TANC1 or TANC2 increases spine and synapse density in cultured neurons and that the effect requires the PDZ-binding C terminus, while the haploinsufficient mouse is reported only as having unspecified synaptic deficits.
nodes.id: Altered Dendritic Spine and Excitatory Synapse Development

evidence.reference_title: Regulation of dendritic spines, spatial memory, and embryonic development by the TANC family of PSD-95-interacting proteins.
evidence.snippet: Overexpression of TANC1 and TANC2 in cultured neurons increases the density of dendritic spines and excitatory synapses in a manner that requires the PDZ (PSD-95/Dlg/ZO-1)-binding C termini of TANC proteins.

nodes.description: More glutamatergic neurons with GABAergic and glycinergic populations unchanged, shifting the balance of the circuit toward excitation. Shown in the zebrafish knockout, which is a complete loss rather than the human heterozygous state.

animal_models.description: The selective expansion of glutamatergic neurons with GABAergic and glycinergic populations unaffected is measured directly in this model.
animal_models.name: tanc2 knockout zebrafish

evidence.reference_title: Knockout of tanc2 causes autism-like behavior and sleep disturbance in zebrafish.
evidence.snippet: We observed that the glutamatergic neuron population is significantly increased in tanc2 mutants while the GABAergic and the glycinergic neurons are not affected, suggesting that an excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) imbalance.

evidence.reference_title: Knockout of tanc2 causes autism-like behavior and sleep disturbance in zebrafish.
evidence.snippet: Loss of tanc2 increases the larval brain size and body length by promoting proliferation and inhibiting apoptosis.

nodes.description: One TANC2 allele lost to a frameshift, nonsense, canonical splice or exon-deletion variant, or to a 17q23.3 copy-number deletion that removes the gene. ClinGen's curation counts twenty-one such variants across twenty-two probands.

evidence.reference_title: TANC2 / intellectual developmental disorder with autistic features and language delay, with or without seizures (Definitive)
evidence.snippet: Twenty-one loss-of-function variants (frameshift, nonsense, splice, and exon deletion) that have been reported in 22 probands in 4 publications

evidence.reference_title: 17q23.3 de novo microdeletion involving only TANC2 gene: A new case.
evidence.snippet: Here, we describe a new case of TANC2 gene disruption in a 17q23.3 de novo microdeletion identified by array-CGH.

nodes.description: The TANC2 brake on mTOR is released. TANC2 inhibits both mTORC1 and mTORC2, in mouse brain and in human neural progenitor cells and neurons, so the loss is not a mouse-only phenomenon.

evidence.reference_title: Tanc2-mediated mTOR inhibition balances mTORC1/2 signaling in the developing mouse brain and human neurons.
evidence.snippet: Lastly, Tanc2 inhibits mTORC1/2 in human neural progenitor cells and neurons.

nodes.description: Dense core vesicles carried by the KIF1A motor are no longer captured at postsynaptic sites. A second synaptic function of TANC2, parallel to the mTOR brake, and one that specific patient mutations abolish.
nodes.id: Loss of KIF1A Dense Core Vesicle Capture at Spines

evidence.reference_title: Regulation of KIF1A-Driven Dense Core Vesicle Transport: Ca(2+)/CaM Controls DCV Binding and Liprin-α/TANC2 Recruits DCVs to Postsynaptic Sites.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, we found that specific TANC2 mutations-reported in patients with different neuropsychiatric disorders-abolish the interaction with KIF1A.

nodes.description: Less of the TANC2 scaffold at excitatory postsynaptic sites. TANC2 is a large multi-domain adaptor expressed mainly in brain, present at synaptic and non-synaptic sites, and interacting directly with PSD-95.
nodes.id: Reduced TANC2 Protein at the Postsynaptic Density

evidence.reference_title: Disruptive mutations in TANC2 define a neurodevelopmental syndrome associated with psychiatric disorders.
evidence.snippet: we report genetic and clinical data for 20 individuals with disruptive mutations in TANC2, a gene encoding a synaptic scaffold protein interacting with multiple ASD and other neuropsychiatric disorder-related postsynaptic density (PSD) proteins in dendrites

evidence.reference_title: Tanc2-mediated mTOR inhibition balances mTORC1/2 signaling in the developing mouse brain and human neurons.
evidence.snippet: Synaptic Tanc2 directly interacts with PSD-95

nodes.description: Epilepsy in about half of reported patients, 11 of 20 in the defining cohort, which is what the "with or without seizures" clause of the disease name records. One subsequent case report describes Lennox-Gastaut syndrome with a de novo nonsense variant, which the authors present as a phenotypic extension rather than a typical presentation.

evidence.reference_title: Disruptive mutations in TANC2 define a neurodevelopmental syndrome associated with psychiatric disorders.
evidence.snippet: In addition to a variable degree of epilepsy and facial dysmorphism

evidence.reference_title: Truncating mutation in TANC2 in a Chinese boy associated with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome: a case report.
evidence.snippet: We described the first Chinese case with LGS associated to a de novo nonsense mutation c.4321C > T(p.Gln1441Ter) in TANC2 gene, which would expand the clinical spectrum related to TANC2 mutations

evidence.reference_title: De novo TANC2 variants caused developmental and epileptic encephalopathy and epilepsy.
evidence.snippet: Patients with null variants exhibited severe phenotypes, including three with epilepsy and neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) and one with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE). In contrast, the patients with missense variants presented with only epilepsy.

nodes.description: The genotype that matches the human disease. It survives, where the homozygous null is embryonic lethal, and shows mTORC1/2 hyperactivity with synaptic and behavioural deficits that rapamycin reverses.
Both mTOR complexes run above their normal level in the haploinsufficient brain. This is the node a therapy would target, and the one rapamycin acts on in the mouse.

animal_models.name: Tanc2 haploinsufficient mouse

evidence.reference_title: Tanc2-mediated mTOR inhibition balances mTORC1/2 signaling in the developing mouse brain and human neurons.
evidence.snippet: Tanc2-haploinsufficient mice survive but display mTORC1/2 hyperactivity accompanying synaptic and behavioral deficits reversed by mTOR-inhibiting rapamycin

nodes.description: A complete knockout that expands the glutamatergic population selectively and shows impaired social preference, increased sleep, anxiolytic behaviour and reduced aggression as an adult.
